Commentary.Commentary: We are back for India's second essay. The two umpires and players have made their way out to the middle. Rohit Sharma and Yashasvi Jaiswal will open the innings for India. Kemar Roach has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...
... THIRD INNINGS ...

West Indies have been rolled over for 255 in their first innings! Mohammed Siraj's five-wicket haul has helped India take a first-innings lead of 183 runs! This has been a collapse of some enormity for the hosts as they have lost their last five wickets for 26 runs. West Indies performed better with the bat than the previous Test but it is still not enough to challenge a side like India. Their openers looked solid and put a 71-run stand. Their skipper, Kraigg led from the front with a gritty 75, and most of their batters got stars but couldn't convert them. Their lower middle order collapsed like nine-pins, putting them on the back foot again as they surrendered a lead of over 180 runs to the visitors. For India, Mohammed Siraj was the star of the show with a brilliant five-wicket haul and he was on fire in this first hour of the morning session. Mukesh Kumar also bowled well on his debut and got a couple of wickets while Jadeja got two scalps too and Ashwin chipped in with one. India find themselves able to dictate the terms in this Test and will look to bat at a swift rate and put West Indies into bat in the third session of Day 4.

Commentary.Commentary: All in readiness for the action to commence on Day 4. The two umpires and Indian players make their way out to the middle amidst blue skies. Let's hope the weather remains the same throughout the day. Out walk the two overnight batters of the West Indies, Alick Athanaze and Jason Holder. It will be Mukesh Kumar to start the proceedings with the ball for India. Off we go...

PITCH REPORT - Daren Ganga is pitchside. Stacy-Ann King joins him and starts by saying that the follow through area is very rough. She adds that the pacers will target this area and that the cracks have opened up as well. Mentions that it will be uncomfortable for the batters in the first period of play. Ganga says that it is not only about seeing off the new ball but the batters need to be careful against the old ball as well.

For India, it was debutant Mukesh Kumar who set the tone for them in the first half of the first session. Jermaine Blackwood and Kraigg Brathwaite stood firm against India's disciplined bowling, but Ravichandran Ashwin, with all his trickery, breached the latter's defence. In the first over, Before the light faded and brought an end to the day's play, Ravindra Jadeja and Mohammed Siraj joined in on the act as well. If India are to force a result here, the first hour on Day 4 will be crucial for them. Can they run through the West Indies' lower order with a ball which is around 5 overs old? Let's find out as the action on Day 4 is coming up shortly.

West Indies's two overnight batters, Kirk Mckenzie and Kraigg Brathwaite, resumed their innings in bright and sunny conditions and looked at ease right from ball one. The debutant departed just before the rain arrived for the first time in the day, bringing an early end to the first session. In the second session, Jermaine Blackwood and Kraigg Brathwaite got together and stitched a gritty stand before being dismissed on either side of the Tea break. Joshua Da Silva fell cheaply as well, but Alick Athanaze and Jason Holder safely negotiated the tricky phase before Stumps. Trailing by 209 runs, the onus is on this pair to get the hosts close to parity.

Hello and a warm welcome, ladies and gentlemen, to our coverage of Day 4 of the second Test between the West Indies and India at Queen's Park Oval in Port of Spain. The first three days of this landmark Test have witnessed both teams grinding it out on a slow surface. As things stand, this game is meandering towards a draw, but if the pitch starts to deteriorate, we are in for two days of captivating action.
... DAY 4, SESSION 1 ...

Right then, We have had a couple of intervals due to rain which has not allowed the moving day of Test cricket to move along at a good pace. West Indies have done well to preserve their wickets but have been far too cautious with their approach This has left the door open for India to get some breakthroughs early in the morning session and set up a win. The action continues on Day 4 of the second Test between West Indies and India on Sunday 23rd July and we have an early start with the first ball being bowled at 7 pm IST (1.30 pm GMT) but you can join us early for the build-up. Cheers!

Alick Athanaze is up for a chat. He starts by saying that he enjoyed batting in Dominica more. Adds that there isn't much spin here as Dominica and that the wicket is slow as well. Reckons that India understood the wicket well and had a proper field setting. On rain interruptions, he says that it is challenging as you have to start all over again. Feels that he and Jason Holder handled it well. Shares that the plan was to get a good stride in and adds that he got a few close calls. Mentions that he is new to the review system hence it was easy to put those calls behind him. Ends by saying that it is all about batting long and sticking to the basics.

Kraigg Brathwaite and Kirk Mckenzie started the day well as they looked comfortable out in the middle with the sun out and the pitch really flat. India had a stroke of luck as Kirk Mckenzie played a loose shot and edged one off the bowling of Mukesh Kumar seconds before rain stopped play for the first time in the day. Early Lunch was taken and we had a full afternoon session played for an extended time as Kraigg Brathwaite built a partnership with his vice-captain Jermaine Blackwood. He reached his half-century in the meantime but received an absolute peach of a delivery from Ravichandran Ashwin and was dismissed for 75 having faced 235 deliveries. West Indies have fought hard in this game which is a massive improvement from their performance in the last fixture but they will need to up the ante if they want to play for a win.

SESSION SUMMARY - 55 runs and 2 wickets in 22 overs. Another rain-interrupted session but the 2 wickets that fell have helped India claim superiority in this game. West Indies were three wickets down when they resumed their inning after Tea. Jermaine Blackwood and Alick Athanaze resumed their partnership after the break but it did not last long as Blackwood edged one to slip off the bowling of Ravindra Jadeja. Ajinkya Rahane took an absolute screamer and when Joshua Da Silva found his stumps shattered by Mohammed Siraj, India felt they had an opening to get a bunch of wickets. Alick Athanaze provided the fight from the hosts as he remained unbeaten on 37 having faced 111 deliveries and has Jason Holder for company. The new ball was taken after 101 overs and the Indian pace bowlers did trouble the batters but were unable to get a breakthrough.

It seems that the umpires have finally decided that the light is not good enough and the players will start walking back to the dressing room. We have had just 67 overs of play today but the game is still up for grabs for India. West Indies have played circumspectly and their scoring rate determines that they are playing for time and looking to draw this game.

OUT! TIMBER! Mohammed Siraj has gone through Joshua Da Silva's defence here! Ishan Kishan had predicted this as the outcome as the rain looked to be arriving! There is a massive gap between the bat and the pad as the ball creeps in and shatters the stumps. The West Indies wicketkeeper looks really disappointed here as he takes the long walk back to the shed! He looks up at the skies as it opens up and the rain comes pouring down. West Indies have lost half their side now and India find themselves back on top in this tie.

Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the third and final session of Day 3. Alick Athanaze and Jermaine Blackwood stride out to the centre to resume their innings and they are joined by the two umpires. The Indian players disperse from their huddle and make their way out to the middle. No new ball for now as Ravindra Jadeja will start the proceedings with the old ball for India. Let's play...
... DAY 3, SESSION 3 ...

As far as India are concerned, they had their tails up, having managed to get rid of the impressive-looking Kirk Mckenzie just before the rain arrived. It was Mukesh Kumar who started the proceedings for India in the second session where he bowled according to the field set for him. India had a ring of fielders in the mid-wicket region against Kraigg Brathwaite but that plan did not bear fruit for them. It was Ravichandran Ashwin who was rewarded for his persistence as he castled Kraigg Brathwaite. The visitors had to be content with only one wicket in the second session but with the second new ball available, India might opt to take it straight away after Tea in their quest for some crucial inroads. Can India manage to break the resistance of the West Indies batters? We shall find out as the players return for the third session at 12.30 am IST (7.00 pm GMT, the previous day) for more intriguing action.

SESSION SUMMARY: 57 runs, 34.2 overs and one wicket. An absorbing session of Test cricket comes to an end! The run-scoring was difficult but West Indies will be pleased, as they did well not lose more than one wicket in the session. At the start of what was an extended second session, the vice-captain Jermaine Blackwood joined skipper Kraigg Brathwaite to solidify the West Indies innings. Both batters showed immense grit and determination against the stump-to-stump bowling ploy by India. Just when both seemed to be at ease out in the middle, a peach of a delivery by Ashwin breached Brathwaite's defence. Playing in only his second Test, Alick Athanaze looked to be positive from ball one and did well not to get bogged down. He, along with Blackwood, safely negotiated the passage before Tea. With West Indies still trailing by 264 runs, they would want this pair to bat the entirety of the third session.

SESSION SUMMARY - 31 runs and 1 wicket in 10.4 overs. West Indies started from where they left off as Kraigg Brathwaite and Kirk Mckenzie looked really solid in the middle. India started off with their pace bowlers who did not trouble the batters much and the West Indian debutant Kirk Mckenzie looked to be growing in confidence as he began scoring freely. The introduction of Ravichandran Ashwin also did not seem to have much of an impact but Mukesh Kumar bowled tight lines to build up pressure from the other end. He was rewarded with a wicket just before it started raining and had the downpour begun 5 seconds earlier, Mukesh Kumar would not have bowled the wicket-taking delivery. The Windies skipper held up one end and is unbeaten on 49 as he hunts for yet another Test half-century. The rain gods have allowed the game to resume in the Old Trafford so till the players take Lunch, you can switch tabs and catch the action in the fourth Ashes Test match. Do join us here at 9.40 pm IST (4.10 pm GMT) to see how the second session of Day 3 plays out.

We have had just less than one hour in the first session and we hope there are no more stoppages throughout the day.

Commentary.Commentary: We are moments away from getting underway here on Day 3. Bright and sunny conditions greet the two umpires as they make their way out to the middle. Out come the two overnight batters of West Indies, Kraigg Brathwaite and Kirk Mckenzie. Indian players are seen in a huddle near the ropes. Rohit Sharma gives some final instructions before the players spread out to take their respective field positions. Jaydev Unadkat will start the proceedings with the ball for India. Here we go...

PITCH REPORT - Daren Ganga is near the deck. He starts by informing that the weather is bright and sunny. He is joined by Curtly Ambrose who starts by saying that this is a very hard surface. Adds that the surface is still good for batting. Mentions that there is wear and tear outside the off stump for right-hander but feels that there is nothing alarming about it. Reckons that the wear and tear on the off stump for left-hander which might pose problems. Ambrose also says that spin is not a real factor and feels that Indian pacers will need to be patient on this wicket. Ganga ends by saying that the bounce has been consistent and is likely to stay the same.

On the flip side, the West Indies started Day 2 slightly on the back foot, but with the second new ball due, they had hopes of restricting India below 350. However, it did not go according to plan for them in the first half of the second session. The hosts clawed their way back into the game to bowl India out in the second session. In reply, Tagenarine Chanderpaul and Kraigg Brathwaite were solid in their approach right from ball one before the former ran out of patience. Kirk Mckenzie has looked positive ever since his arrival and will look to start afresh with his skipper. Will either team manage to wrestle the advantage on this moving day? Stick around to find out.

Having begun Day 2 at the overnight score of 288-4, a special century by Virat Kohli in his 500th international game, and fifties by Ravindra Jadeja and Ravichandran Ashwin, India managed to post 438 in their first innings. India's bowlers were riding high on confidence courtesy of the clinical display at Dominica, but they were made to work hard on this slow surface. As he always does, Ravindra Jadeja broke the flourishing opening stand, which brought some respite late in the day to the visitors. If the wicket continues to play slow, Indian bowlers are in for a long day's work.

Hello and a warm welcome, ladies and gentlemen, to our coverage of Day 3 of the second Test between the West Indies and India at Queen's Park Oval in Port of Spain. Unlike the first Test, where the West Indies failed to show up, the hosts have shown the stomach for a fight in the second Test, and hence, this game hangs in the balance as we arrive at the moving day.
... DAY 3, SESSION 1 ...

Right then, the game is nicely poised after an intriguing day of cricket. West Indies managed to bowl out India and have gotten off to a good start with the bat. We now move to Day 3 in this second Test match and the moving day of Test cricket is bound to be full of thrills. Both teams have a good opportunity to shift the tide in their favor and it is to be seen which team takes the initiative. There is more action coming our way on Friday 22nd July and the first ball of Day 3 will be bowled at 7.30 pm IST (2 pm GMT) but you can join us early for the build-up. Cheers!

Virat Kohli is in for a flash interview. He says that he enjoyed himself out in the middle. Adds that he was in the rhythm and wanted to be in. Mentions that it was challenging at the start. Shares that he gets charged up when there is something to overcome. States that he had to be patient as the outfield was slow. Feels satisfied as he had done the hard yards. Mentions that he looks to focus on what he has to do for the team. On his 500th international game, he says that he feels grateful to play 500 games for India. Adds that he has looked after himself through his training and diet. On the 100th Test between India and West Indies, he says that it is a special occasion as India and West Indies go a long way. Feels that he could not have asked for a better start to this Test. Also says that Antigua and Queen's Park Oval are two of his favourite venues in the West Indies. Reckons that the wicket is on the slower side and feels that if they manage to keep the pressure on, they will get wickets.

India started the day four wickets down with Virat Kohli and Ravindra Jadeja at the crease and 288 runs on the board. The two Indian batters looked comfortable out in the middle and added 159 runs for the fifth wicket. Virat reached his 29th Test century and Jadeja notched up a half-century as it looked like India would post a mammoth first-inning total. Alzarri Joseph managed to break the partnership with a direct hit as he got Virat run out for 121 and Kemar Roach dismissed Jadeja soon after. Jason Holder dismissed Ishan Kishan after Lunch and Jomel Warrican managed to take a double-strike to send Jaydev Unadkat and Mohammed Siraj back to the shed. Ravichandran Ashwin scored a half-century to push India to 438 before being bowled by Kemar Roach. The Indians would have liked a few more runs on a pitch that has suited the batters and with the start West Indies have, they will be hoping the spinners can come into play as the game progresses.

SESSION SUMMARY - 86 runs and 1 wicket in 41 overs. West Indies have fought exceedingly well with the bat and have kept themselves well in this tie with a hard-fought final session. They started their batting effort post the Tea break and the openers battled it out to negotiate the new ball. Kraigg Brathwaite and Tagenarine Chanderpaul started slow looking to see how the pitch would play and soaked in the pressure put by the Indian bowlers. The two of them added a 71-run partnership in 208 balls till one false shot by Chanderpaul resulted in his demise. Ravindra Jadeja had not bowled at him in the 6 overs till then and it took him two deliveries to dismiss the left-hander. Kirk Mckenzie looked nervous out in the middle on his debut but survived till Stumps and the hosts will look to continue the good work on Day 3. The Indian bowlers have been economical but they will know that wickets are the name of the game.

Brathwaite survives a scare on the last ball of the day! Jadeja bowls a loopy delivery, on off and middle, Kraigg Brathwaite looks to get to the pitch of the ball and loses sight of the ball. The ball sneaks through the bat and pad gap. Luckily for him, Ishan Kishan fails to grab the ball cleanly. It would not have mattered anyway though as Brathwaite had got his bat back in the crease. That will be Stumps on Day 2!
